A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed an organoid model for human liver development that recapitulates the molecular signatures of fetal liver development, which can be used to study the molecular mechanisms of organogenesis.

we have reconstructed the lineage progression of hepatocytes from pluripotential stem cells in two-dimensional culture and we have then used this to guide the development of a three-dimensional organoid system that recapitulates the heterotypic interactions that occur during liver development.

we used single-cell RNA sequencing and three-dimensional organoid technology to reconstruct liver development from pluripotent stem cells, and to identify signalling mechanisms that drive hepatoblast differentiation in human liver buds.
The main takeaway from our work is that
three-dimensional organoids recapitulate the molecular and cellular complexity of organ development, and that heterotypic interactions are essential for lineage progression.
the liver buds we generate recapitulate many of the features of fetal liver development.
heterotypic interactions between cell types are critical for the development of complex tissues and organs.
